question_text: Distinguish between centre of mass and centre of gravity.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: Number the points — the matching pair on the other side must line up one for one.
steps.why: The centre of mass is pure geometry-of-mass: it exists even far from any planet, which is exactly what point 2 records.
common_mistakes: Writing prose instead of numbered points, so nothing lines up with the other column.

recall.must_convey: That the centre of mass concentrates the MASS, is independent of g, and governs translation.
accept: whole mass concentrated at a point
reject: whole weight acts at that point

steps.memory_tip: Centre of MASS: the mass average — it exists even in deep space, with no gravity at all.

steps.label: Centre of gravity
lines: 1. The point through which the whole
2. It depends on the value of g.
3. It decides the stability and balance

lines.text: 4. For a small body in a uniform field,
it coincides with the centre of mass.

steps.margin_note: Point 4 is the connecting sentence examiners look for: for ordinary bodies the two points coincide.
steps.why: Weight is mass TIMES g — so wherever g varies across a very large body, the weight-average and the mass-average part company. For everything on a table top they are the same point.
common_mistakes: Claiming the two are always different. For a small uniform-field body they coincide.

recall.must_convey: That the centre of gravity is where the weight acts, depends on g, and coincides with the CM for small bodies.
accept: whole weight acts at that point
reject: whole mass concentrated at a point

steps.memory_tip: Centre of GRAVITY: the weight average — the two points separate only where g varies across the body.
